transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-02
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 39 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood Marketing); Rachel Kim (Novainsights, Head of ML), Daniel Ortega (CTO), Priya Singh (Product Lead)

Summary:
Quick podcast-style interview focusing on Novainsights' experience with Redwood Inference: migration path, performance wins, cost impact, and a few customer quotes for a case study. We recorded audio for marketing; agreed to minor edits and transcript review.

Topics Covered:
- Why Novainsights chose Redwood (cost, latency, deployment flexibility)
- Migration story (hosted -> dedicated for production)
- Measured improvements (latency, throughput, cost per 1M tokens)
- Security/compliance notes (KMS, SOC2, VPC)
- Next steps for case study and distribution

00:00:05 - Avery: Hey everyone, welcome. This is the Redwood customer chat with Novainsights. Thanks so much for joining; we'll keep this informal, record, and Maya will edit for the podcast, so we'll send a draft.
00:00:18 - Rachel: Great, thanks for having us. Excited to share a bit about how we've been using Redwood.
00:00:24 - Daniel: Hi all.
00:00:27 - Priya: Morning.

00:01:02 - Avery: Maybe to kick us off — Rachel, can you tell the listeners a quick 15‑30 sec on what Novainsights does and the product team focus?
00:01:15 - Rachel: Sure. Uh, Novainsights is, like, a data insights platform for retail analytics: we do demand forecasting, product analytics, and a big piece is natural language Q&A for non-technical users. So our product team was trying to make the self-serve analytics more conversational, right, so product managers can ask, like, "show me seasonality for sku 1234" and get charts and explanations.
00:01:48 - Daniel: And we wanted that to be low latency; our dashboard is interactive so anything above 400–500ms felt laggy.

00:02:22 - Samir: When did you first start evaluating LLM providers and what were the hard constraints?
00:02:31 - Rachel: We started late 2024. Constraints were: sub-500ms median latency for short prompts, predictable cost for high volume, and data controls — some of our customers require logs not be retained beyond X days. We also had an internal ownership question — do we build our own stack or pick a managed inference partner.
00:03:00 - Priya: And timeline-wise, we needed something in prod by Q2 2025 for a large retail customer pilot.

00:03:22 - Avery: That's helpful. Can you talk about why you picked Redwood? Any concerns initially?
00:03:29 - Rachel: Yeah, two things: the performance profiles you published were very close to our workload patterns — the 1k seq-length quantized profiles matched our interactive prompts, and the routing/fallback story was compelling. Second, the Dedicated offering meant we could get predictable throughput for the pilot. Our main concerns were security and egress cost.
00:04:05 - Daniel: Also the cost math. We ran comparisons vs OpenAI and a couple of self-host options. Redwood's batching and KV cache recommendations reduced our per-token compute by like 30% in tests — those numbers mattered.

00:04:46 - Samir: Nice. Can you share any concrete numbers you feel comfortable with for the case study?
00:04:55 - Rachel: Mm, yes. In our pilot we moved to Redwood Dedicated in Jan 2025. Our 95th percentile latency for the interactive Q&A dropped from ~620ms to ~310ms. Throughput increased — tokens/sec improved about 2.1x under concurrent users. Cost per 1M tokens, after applying recommended quantization and caching, dropped roughly 28%.
00:05:32 - Priya: And subjective quality was stable; we didn't see hallucination increases after quantization once prompts were tuned.

00:06:00 - Maya: That's a great quote, Rachel — "latency cut in half, cost down nearly 30%" — can we use that exact phrasing in the case study?
00:06:08 - Rachel: Yep, fine by me.

00:06:35 - Avery: There are sometimes questions about vendor lock-in — did you do any canary or A/B tests to compare fallback behavior?
00:06:45 - Daniel: We did. We ran Redwood hosted as a canary initially and then moved to Dedicated regionally. The smart routing was nice because during peak days Redwood routed to a slightly larger variant and we didn't have to build that orchestration ourselves. We also maintained a self-host fallback for a subset of low-priority workloads — mostly to keep the option — but we haven't had to flip to it in production.

00:07:25 - Samir: Security & compliance — there will be listeners curious. What did you require and did Redwood meet it?
00:07:33 - Rachel: Key things were SOC 2, SSO/SAML with role-based access, KMS integration for encryption at rest, and retention controls. Redwood's Private and Dedicated contracts, plus the audit logs and KMS options, checked the boxes. We had a few clarifying Qs on retention windows and Avery's team provided the security pack which answered them.

00:08:10 - Avery: Glad that helped. Were there any surprises in onboarding?
00:08:15 - Priya: Mostly pleasant. The onboarding took about three weeks to get from trial to Dedicated provisioning — there were a few infra adjustments in our VPC but the Redwood SE team helped. Samir actually did the initial perf run with us which helped tune batching and KV cache settings to our prompt mix.
00:08:39 - Samir: I remember wresting with one prompt that was heavy on tokens; we ended up splitting it and using structured output which cut token count.
00:08:49 - Rachel: Yeah that saved a lot.

00:09:20 - Maya: For the podcast listeners, can you share a short anecdote — like a user story where this change actually mattered?
00:09:29 - Rachel: Sure. A buyer at a retail chain used our conversational dashboard during a live inventory review and asked for supply risk across 50 SKUs. Previously the report timed out if they attempted that in one query; with Redwood the interactive session returned sub-second answers and the buyer could drill in live. They ended up adding Novainsights to their vendor shortlist because of that demo.
00:09:58 - Priya: That demo directly influenced a pilot conversion later that month.

00:10:20 - Daniel: On the product side, the stability under load and the transparent cost metrics from the Console were big for us. Being able to see token-level cost by route made budgeting easier.

00:10:45 - Avery: Any hesitations about public case study — logos, numbers, or quotes we should avoid?
00:10:51 - Rachel: We're fine with high-level numbers and quotes. We asked not to publish individual customer names that were in our demos, and to avoid showing raw PII examples. Otherwise good.

00:11:20 - Maya: Noted. We'll anonymize those parts. We'll send a one-page draft and the edited audio.

00:11:35 - Samir: Quick tech question for listeners — did you use quantized models in production and any perf/quality trade-offs?
00:11:43 - Priya: Yes, 4-bit quantized for most routes. We preserved some layers in higher precision for critical prompts; after A/B prompting we didn't see quality regressions. The guidance from Redwood on which layers to keep higher precision was useful.

00:12:10 - Avery: Great. Any closing tips for teams considering Redwood?
00:12:16 - Rachel: Do a short pilot with realistic prompts and traffic. Use the batching and KV cache guidance early — it really moves the needle. And, align on retention policies with your security team before launch.

00:12:44 - Daniel: Add the Console metrics to your ops dashboard early so your finance team isn't surprised by token usage.

00:13:02 - Maya: Perfect. We'll wrap up with next steps.

00:13:10 - Avery: Recap — we'll (1) edit the audio and send the draft transcript by next week, (2) Maya will draft a one-page case study, (3) Samir will share performance spreadsheet and notes. Anything else?
00:13:25 - Rachel: Nope that's good. Thanks!

00:13:35 - Priya: Thanks everyone.

00:13:40 - Daniel: Appreciate it.

00:13:55 - End of recording.
